gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patient previously diagnosed with WHO grade 4 IDH-wildtype GBM, determined through genomic and/or histopathological analysis.

candidate_evidence.quote: Treatment dosing will be 200mg of pembrolizumab every three weeks for up to six months or until disease progression, whichever occurs first.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: 6-8 patients with recurrent glioblastoma and identified mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency will be administered pembrolizumab along with focused ultrasound sonication following surgery for recurrent glioblastoma

role_evidence.quote: Pembrolizumab along with focused ultrasound sonication following surgery for recurrent glioblastoma.

Post Pembro infusion, patients will received NaviFUS sonication to the complete volume of the tumor resection bed (as limited by anatomic constraints relative to the tumor extension) following microbubble (Bracco Imaging, SonoVue® or Lumason®; 0.1 mL/Kg; maximum 4.8 mL) administration

agents.drug_class_hint: sulfur hexafluoride lipid microbubble ultrasound contrast agent, used with focused ultrasound

source_quote.quote: MMR deficiencies confirmed per standard of care immunohistochemical analysis or Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) of the patient's surgical sample from the time of initial GBM diagnosis or recurrence.

coder_notes: MMR deficiency is an entry requirement and is mechanistically linked to the anti-PD-1 candidate pembrolizumab (checkpoint inhibitor in hypermutated/MMR-deficient tumours), so candidate_matched true. Pembrolizumab coded device_dependent because it is given with microbubble-enhanced focused ultrasound sonication after infusion; the record does not explicitly say 'BBB opening', but FUS plus microbubbles after drug infusion is focused-ultrasound-enabled delivery. The microbubble is described only inside the device intervention text; listed as delivery_enabling_agent (moiety sulfur hexafluoride inferred from SonoVue/Lumason brand). Exploratory PD-L1/MSI/TMB rows: candidate_matched left false because they are correlative only (not entry requirements). NaviFUS Corporation is collaborator; no text says drug supplied by a company. Regimen monotherapy: pembrolizumab is the only antitumour drug and no radiotherapy in the experimental arm (FUS is a device).
